newsitem.title: LATVIA: UNIBANKA SHAREHOLDERS SAY NO TO MERGER.
newsitem.headline: UNIBANKA SHAREHOLDERS SAY NO TO MERGER.

text.p: The shareholders of Latvia's Unibanka on Monday rejected a proposed merger with Zemes Bank and approved in principle a Eurobond issue, shareholders said.

The shareholders' meeting supported a draft resolution of the Swedfund, one of its leading stock holders, saying the two banks would bring more benefit to their owners if they continued operations as separate entities, a shareholder told Reuters.
The synergies of a possible merger were not as big as expected, the shareholders said.
The meeting also agreed in principle on a eurobond issue and a public share issue.
"The meeting decided to issue ordinary and bearer shares whose total value should not be twice as big as the paid basic capital," a shareholder said.
The board of the bank was entrusted with working out the rules of the eurobond issue and the prospectus for the public issue, he added.
Unibanka, Latvia's second largest bank, had been exploring the possibility of merging with Zemes Bank, Latvia's eight largest bank, since last year.
But two of Unibanka's largest shareholders, Swedfund and the European bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD), earlier this year said that the merger did not look like a good idea.
Of the bank's major shareholders, only the state, which has a 33 percent stake, supported the merger.
Unibanka in March said it was planning a small eurobond issue by the middle of 1997. The issue would be small by eurobond markets, where issues normally start at $50 million, the bank said.
